tools: ten review subagents over the combined diff plus two adversarial verifiers per finding
limitations: npm audit cannot run: no dependencies and no lockfile (C-10 unverified, not required)
no UI in this repository; visual review is not applicable

this repository is deliberately not migrated (PRD v5 section 9, PRD v6 section 3), so its own evidence is an authored schema 1 manifest written with the pinned released v0.5.0 kit; schema 2 and schema 3 evidence are demonstrated in fixtures and the replay cases
live observation covers Claude Code print mode with Sonnet on macOS only; interactive mode, Codex, Copilot, the plugin install and Windows are untested live
no live trial adopted strict coverage: the benchmark briefs are single-change tasks and adoption is opt-in, so the strict path is covered by the suites and the replay cases, not by a live session
the stale-lock reclaim window in state.cjs was reported by review and could not be reproduced (20x8 and 25x32 concurrent writers, all clean); it is carried as an open thread, not as a verified defect

the escaped-regression measure of the delivery benchmark is the candidate own npm test for five of six briefs; docs/delivery-benchmark.md describes it more broadly and is inside the freeze, so the discrepancy is recorded in docs/trial-prd-v6.md rather than corrected

this manifest is the evaluation of the selected PRD, v6. The candidate also carries PRD v5 (T-47..T-65), whose per-requirement dispositions are recorded in NOTES.md and mapped per scenario in docs/prd-v5-review-packet.md, not in a second manifest: the runtime admits only the named manifest own listed artifacts as a post-candidate change, so a second manifest would make this evaluation read stale. PRD v5 therefore has an authored and reviewed disposition record but not a validator-checked one.

coverage_review: Every R-01..R-10 of .prd/prd-v6.md maps to its tickets and to C-01 (the 51-suite chain, which carries the fault-injection cases for each scenario), C-07 (the CI matrix on this candidate) and C-11 (the review record). docs/prd-v6-review-packet.md carries the per-scenario table, and its validator now binds those citations to the repository rather than to prose (T-86): a ticket citation must be that ticket's own commit, and every scenario row must cite a tagged suite. This candidate was reviewed by ten subagents over disjoint areas, each finding reproduced before it was reported and the fourteen most severe adversarially verified by two independent refuters; thirty-two findings were raised, thirteen confirmed, one refuted, and eight fix tickets (T-79..T-86) close every confirmed defect with a regression test that was mutation-checked against its own fix. Whether those suites are adequate proof of the runtime is my judgment as evaluator: they drive real subprocesses and assert on real on-disk state, and the mutation testing recorded in C-11 is the basis for that judgment.

requirements.note: every paragraph of a multi-paragraph scenario now belongs to that scenario, so changed scenario behaviour changes its digest (T-84)
affected is scenario-derived by the frozen contract; per-scenario attribution is restored by T-84
the independent validator refuses an undeclared check link, a candidate whose PRD blob is unreadable, and an invented authorization (T-83)
adoption is explicit and old runtimes reject the new schemas; the ticket guard no longer lets an allowlisted verb carry a shell write into the newly protected paths (T-81)
the reports are complete through a pipe (T-79) and route to a command the runtime accepts in every lifecycle state (T-80)
the benchmark ran and every number recomputes from the saved records; the trial record now states what those runs do and do not establish (T-82)
